title: Data Governance in Cricket: How Delhi Capitals Could Use Analytics Responsibly
dek: Analytics is only as good as the data under it. An audit of the warehouse behind this series shows what Delhi Capitals, or anyone, can and cannot responsibly claim from it.
excerpt: The CricField warehouse is strong on the essentials and has clear gaps: some fields are empty, some are sparse, and some live only in side files. Responsible analytics starts by publishing that audit.

sections.heading: Why Governance Comes First
body: A club using analytics makes decisions about players' careers. That carries a duty to know what the data can support, to say what it cannot, and to protect any personal data it holds.
This audit covers the warehouse behind every article in this series.

sections.heading: What the Audit Found
body: {{ev:dg-len}} of deliveries carry a length tag, but only {{ev:dg-spd}} carry a speed. The stored required-run-rate field is non-zero for {{ev:dg-rrr}} of deliveries, player of the match is recorded for {{ev:dg-potm}} of matches, and the partnerships table has {{ev:dg-part}} rows.
Nationality is known for {{ev:dg-cty}} of players in the players table. The chart summarises coverage field by field.

sections.heading: How This Series Handles the Gaps
body: Where a stored field is empty, the series recomputes it from ball-by-ball data (required rates, partnerships) or avoids it (player of the match). Nationality and birth dates come from separate player-bio files, with coverage stated in every article that uses them.

sections.heading: Proposal: Principles for a Franchise
body: Proposal: publish a coverage audit with every analysis, recompute rather than trust derived fields, state sample sizes, keep personal data such as medical and fitness records separate and access-controlled, and give players sight of the metrics used to judge them.
These are standard data-governance practices applied to cricket.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Show the Gaps
body: Delhi Capitals, and every analyst, should publish what their data does not contain alongside what it shows.
An honest audit is the cheapest guard against confident mistakes.
